entries.title: Braillix — a refreshable Braille display for mathematics (software half)
entries.summary: The teacher's blackboard on a blind child's fingers: a maths teacher writes, types or photographs a lesson and it lands on refreshable braille cells, live and verified, in English and Hindi — no account, no server, no API key, offline after first load. Capstone project; software built with a five-person team.

bullets.text: Built the on-device recognition pipeline that turns handwriting, typed maths and textbook photos into Nemeth braille — Tesseract for English and Hindi words, a 76 MB on-device formula model for maths — with nothing leaving the room
Verified the syllabus live: all 232 curriculum lines from classes 1–12, arithmetic to Bayes' theorem, translate and read back cleanly in about a second on the production site

Engineered 3 independent proofs per expression so every dot can be trusted — Nemeth from speech-rule-engine over MathML, golden vectors against published tables, and a hand-rolled readback engine that reconstructs meaning from the dots alone
Reduced press-to-result from 64 s to about 1.25 s by warming both recognisers in the background at app start

Designed the hardware transport as 1 interface with 3 implementations (simulator, Web Serial USB, Wi-Fi pods) under one conformance suite, plus a virtual pod that speaks the whole protocol so integration day starts from working
Shipped with 727 unit tests and 101 end-to-end journeys; the build fails if any recognition model, OCR language file or Nemeth table is missing from the artifact

evidence.note: Public repo + live deployment; README read 05-Sep-2026 (232-line syllabus proof, 727 unit / 101 e2e tests, ~1.25 s scan).

context.problem: A maths teacher who only knows WhatsApp needs a blackboard that lands on a blind student's fingers, live and verified, in English and Hindi.
features: One surface: the lesson as typeset chalk, the cells beneath, a chalk tray with every symbol a school line needs
Write it like chalk · type it like a message · photograph it — all read on the laptop, offline
Nothing recognised reaches the display without a human: the confirm gate is a TypeScript type
Many students, one lesson: pods of different sizes mirror the same cells

entries.title: Sehat Saarthi — Punjabi-first AI screening co-pilot for government hospitals
entries.summary: A Punjabi-first, fully free, multi-disease screening co-pilot for Punjab's government hospitals — the doctor drives, the saarthi guides. Proof of concept, pending clinical validation.

bullets.text: Trained 9 disease-screening modules on public datasets and deployed only the 7 a doctor can trust after a written reliability analysis — heart disease ROC-AUC 0.948, chest X-ray 0.957, breast cancer 0.998; retinopathy at 0.686 kept out

Designed the whole product Punjabi-first across 7 live modules: Gurmukhi primary on every element, Web Speech read-outs for low-literacy patients, and a printable bilingual referral slip for the paper workflow rural clinics actually use

Built the three-layer free stack — a Vite frontend on Vercel, FastAPI on a Hugging Face Space, tiny .joblib and .onnx models bundled in the package — with a module router so adding a disease is configuration, never a rewrite
Tuned every model high-recall with a mandatory bilingual disclaimer and an honest recall note; the service degrades to a deterministic stub instead of crashing when a model is missing

evidence.note: Public repo + live app + HF Space API; README and model cards read 05-Sep-2026.

context.problem: Punjab's tier-2/3 bottleneck is detection, not treatment: vacant specialist posts, no labs, India's highest Hepatitis-C burden, low-literacy Punjabi-only patients.
features: Seven live modules with per-module Model Cards and honest limitations
Decision-support, never diagnosis: probability + confidence, three bands, high-recall
Punjab palette + phulkari motif, built for a cheap Android on flaky internet

entries.title: Sifarish — a job-hunt chief of staff that refuses to lie
entries.summary: A personal team of agents for one candidate: an evidence ledger compiled into a truth-checked résumé and cover letter per job posting, lawful worldwide job discovery, an apply cockpit and a pipeline board — fully functional with zero API keys.

bullets.text: Architected the truth-compiler: every résumé line carries ledger evidence ids, the LLM may rephrase but never mint, and the PDF's text layer is parse-back-tested 100% against the compiled lines on every export
Built lawful discovery over 29 keyless ATS boards plus aggregator APIs across 18 country markets, with a work-authorization verdict at ingest — never scraping, never auto-submitting

Built a free-tier LLM router (Gemini and Groq, JSON-schema strict) with a deterministic fallback behind every feature, and a strategist pass that reads a whole posting into what the company values before it plans the page
Enforced 776 automated gates including a 5,000-case generated-input matrix, an encrypted cross-device vault, and a read-only demo that cannot spend a token

evidence.note: Public repo + live deployment; 1st place, Agentic & GenAI showcase, Techgyan Hackathon, IIT Ropar.

context.problem: Off-campus applying at scale needs a résumé tailored per company without a single invented claim, and a hunt that finds fresh, eligible roles lawfully.
features: Compile truth. Draft everything. Send nothing.
Ek Baat: talk to the team — ledger adds, vision edits, hunts — proposed, you confirm
Apply Cockpit: pre-flight mistake-proofing + an autofill bookmarklet that structurally cannot submit

entries.title: Aaina — an honest, research-grounded reading of a relationship
entries.summary: Free, no account: 122 questions drawn from published psychological research, 14 scored dimensions, a report written from the tensions between a person's own answers, and a plan of published exercises chosen for the results.

bullets.text: Enforced anti-generic output in code: the model receives only an evidence bundle (scores, tensions, quoted answers), must cite evidence ids per paragraph under a strict JSON schema, and any paragraph whose evidence does not resolve is discarded before rendering
Measured the anti-generic guarantee: 5 genuinely different profiles through the live model produced 0 identical sentences across all 10 pairs, in a re-runnable proof script
Scored 14 dimensions from published instruments (CSI, Investment Model Scale, ECR-S, CPQ, Partner Phubbing Scale) and sequenced goodwill work before conflict work, following the intervention evidence
Implemented the harm screen as memory-only by construction — never stored, transmitted or printed — with a quick-exit button and verified Indian helplines shown first

evidence.note: Public repo + live app; README and PROOF-ANTI-GENERIC.md read 05-Sep-2026.

context.problem: Most relationship advice is written for nobody in particular.
features: The contradiction engine: the report is written from tensions between a person's own answers
Every prescribed activity is a published intervention with mechanism, evidence grade and contraindications

entries.title: Spark Core — a portfolio that evolves itself
entries.summary: A running system, not a snapshot: it watches my GitHub, absorbs new repos, writes its own case studies from their READMEs, and logs its own evolution on the page.

bullets.text: Designed GitHub as the database: a manifest committed through the contents API drives every project, skill and line of copy across 5 env-only secrets; a referee test fails the build if a component contains personal content or a token-like string
Built the Cortex: one tap reads a repo's README and Groq writes a strict-JSON case study that is committed and versioned — grounded in the README, never regenerated per visit
Built an authenticated evolve seam (Bearer secret) so other systems can teach the portfolio new skills; edits go live in ~60 s with no redeploy

evidence.note: Public repo + live site; README read 05-Sep-2026.

context.problem: Portfolios go stale the day after they are built.
features: Nothing is hardcoded that can be lived — component code contains zero personal content
